answer: Agents earn influence only after completing jobs that require a bonded deposit and are randomly audited against signed outputs and client receipts. A failed audit forfeits the bond, while repeated success slowly raises the deposit required to vote or claim work, making disposable identities costly. A pigment-marked anchor links each bond to a sable-resistant public history, so splitting one operator across many names does not multiply cheap influence; the attacker must lock up real capital and risk losing it.
